name: Alabama
text: Alabama has one of the latest and most spread-out ruts in the country. Depending on where you hunt, peak breeding can land anywhere from early December to late January, and some areas run into February. Much of the variation traces back to where each area's deer were restocked from in the 1900s.
zones: Much of central and west Alabama
Parts of south and southwest Alabama

name: Alaska
text: Alaska's deer are Sitka black-tailed deer, found mainly in the Southeast and on Kodiak. Their rut typically peaks from late October through November.

name: Arizona
text: Arizona's Coues whitetail rut is one of the latest in the West, typically peaking from mid December into mid January. Desert mule deer generally rut in December and January as well.
zones: December into January, varying by unit

name: Arkansas
text: State conception studies place peak breeding in mid to late November across most of Arkansas, with parts of the south and the Delta running later.

name: California
text: California's deer are mostly black-tailed and mule deer, and rut timing varies widely by region and elevation. Coastal blacktails often rut from October into November, while mule deer in the mountains and east side typically rut in November.

name: Colorado
text: Colorado's mule deer rut typically peaks from mid November into early December. Whitetails on the eastern plains generally peak in mid to late November.

name: Connecticut
text: Connecticut's peak breeding typically falls in the second half of November, with southern and coastal areas running a few days later than the north.

name: Delaware
text: Delaware's rut typically peaks around the middle of November across the state.

name: Florida
text: Florida has the most variable rut in the country. State conception studies show breeding as early as July in parts of South Florida and as late as February in the Panhandle. Always go by your own area, not a statewide date.
zones: Can be as early as July through September
Varies widely, often late summer through fall

name: Georgia
text: Georgia's rut varies a lot from county to county. Much of the state sees breeding activity from late October through November, but timing shifts by region and some areas run later. Georgia DNR publishes a county-by-county rut map built from deer-vehicle collision data.
zones: Varies by county; check the DNR rut map

name: Hawaii
text: Hawaii has no native deer. Introduced axis deer can breed year-round, so there's no single rut season.

name: Idaho
text: Idaho's whitetail and mule deer ruts typically peak in mid to late November, with the Panhandle running slightly earlier than the Clearwater and southern units.

name: Illinois
text: Illinois conception studies center peak breeding around November 10, with southern Illinois running a little later than the north.

name: Indiana
text: Indiana's peak breeding typically falls in the first half of November, roughly November 6 to 14 in most years.

name: Iowa
text: Iowa's rut typically peaks during the first three weeks of November, a bit earlier in the north than the south.

name: Kansas
text: Kansas whitetails typically peak in mid November, with the south running a few days behind the north.

name: Kentucky
text: Kentucky's rut typically peaks in mid November statewide, with western Kentucky sometimes running slightly later.

name: Louisiana
text: Louisiana's rut swings widely by area. State conception studies show breeding from late September in some southern parishes through February in others. Check the timing for your specific area.
zones: Can be as early as fall or as late as February

name: Maine
text: Maine's rut typically peaks in mid November, with northern and western areas running earlier than the south and coast.

name: Maryland
text: Maryland's rut typically peaks in the first half to middle of November, with western Maryland a little earlier than the Eastern Shore.

name: Massachusetts
text: Massachusetts peak breeding typically runs from about November 6 to 20.

name: Michigan
text: Michigan's rut typically peaks in early to mid November, starting earlier in the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula.

name: Minnesota
text: Minnesota's rut typically peaks in early to late November, with the north ahead of the south.

name: Mississippi
text: Mississippi's rut is late and varies by region. Breeding generally runs from December into February, and the average in far southeast Mississippi can be about five weeks later than in parts of the Delta. MDWFP publishes a statewide breeding date map.

name: Missouri
text: Missouri's rut typically peaks in mid November, with southern Missouri a few days behind the north.

name: Montana
text: Montana's whitetail and mule deer ruts typically peak in mid to late November.

name: Nebraska
text: Nebraska's whitetail rut typically peaks in mid November, slightly earlier in the east than the west, and mule deer run toward late November.

name: Nevada
text: Nevada's deer are mule deer, and their rut typically peaks from late November into mid December.

name: New Hampshire
text: New Hampshire's rut typically peaks over about three weeks starting in mid November, with the North Country running earlier.

name: New Jersey
text: New Jersey conception studies put peak breeding from early to late November, with southern New Jersey slightly later than the north.

name: New Mexico
text: New Mexico's mule deer rut typically peaks in December, and Coues whitetails in the southwest can run into January.

name: New York
text: New York's rut typically peaks in mid November, starting earlier in the north and running later on Long Island.
zones: Northern New York and the Adirondacks
Southern Tier, Hudson Valley and Long Island

name: North Carolina
text: North Carolina's rut varies by region. State conception data show peak breeding ranging from around the end of October in parts of the east to early December in the western mountains.

name: North Dakota
text: North Dakota's rut typically peaks in mid November, generally around November 15 to 20.

name: Ohio
text: Ohio's rut typically peaks in the first half to middle of November statewide.

name: Oklahoma
text: Oklahoma's rut typically peaks in the second and third weeks of November, with the south sometimes running later.

name: Oregon
text: Oregon's blacktail and mule deer ruts typically peak in November, with whitetails in the northeast peaking in mid November.

name: Pennsylvania
text: Pennsylvania's conception studies put peak breeding in mid November across most of the state, slightly earlier in the north.

name: Rhode Island
text: Rhode Island's rut typically peaks in mid November, centered around November 14.

name: South Carolina
text: South Carolina has one of the earliest ruts in the country. Breeding typically runs from mid to late October through mid November, though timing varies by area.

name: South Dakota
text: South Dakota's whitetail rut typically peaks in mid November, a bit earlier east of the Missouri River than west.

name: Tennessee
text: Tennessee's rut typically peaks in November, running from east to west, with West Tennessee and some southern counties later.

name: Texas
text: Texas rut timing depends heavily on region. State conception studies show breeding from late summer to February. Generally, the Hill Country and central Texas peak in November, while South Texas runs from mid December into January.

name: Utah
text: Utah's deer are mostly mule deer, and their rut typically peaks from mid November into early December.

name: Vermont
text: Vermont's rut typically peaks in mid November, centered around November 15, with the north slightly ahead.

name: Virginia
text: Virginia's rut typically peaks in mid November, with some southern and southeastern counties running later.

name: Washington
text: Washington's ruts typically peak in November: whitetails in the northeast in mid November, and mule deer and blacktails in mid to late November.

name: West Virginia
text: West Virginia's rut typically peaks in mid to late November.

name: Wisconsin
text: Wisconsin's rut typically peaks in early to mid November, with the northern forest running ahead of southern farmland.

name: Wyoming
text: Wyoming's mule deer and whitetail ruts typically peak from mid November into early December.
